newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty hits low vs dollar, dips vs currency basket.
newsitem.headline: Zloty hits low vs dollar, dips vs currency basket.

text.p: The zloty eased against the basket of currencies and fell to an all-time low against the U.S. dollar, pushed down by a morning currency-buy trend caused by foreigners selling Polish treasuries, dealers said.

They said these small-scale orders sparked some additional currency purchases, which sank the zloty as players were keen on lengthening currency positions after last week's central bank dollar- and mark-buying interventions left many short.
"The zloty hit its all-time low below 3.0000 dollars on this morning's small sales of Polish treasuries by foreigners," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 2.07/1.98 percent from the parity rate, down than Friday's 2.31/2.25 percent. It closed at 3.0035/55 to the dollar, down from 2.9895/15 on Friday and at 1.8340/60 to the mark, down from 1.8330/40.

The central bank fixed the zloty weaker at 1.99 percent from the weighted dollar and mark parity rates from Friday's 2.19 percent, which some dealers said was low enough to again spark foreign investor purchases of Polish treasuries.
"If it turns out the central bank does not intervene at present levels, then foreigners could again come and push the zloty higher," said Piotr Czyzewski of ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said foreigners only bought several million zlotys worth of paper at Monday's 800 million zloty T-bill auction.
Minimum prices of all T-bills fell 0.01 point at the tender on total demand of 694 million zlotys.
Interbank deposit rates eased during the session after the central bank refrained from draining the market on Monday.
Overnight rates were quoted at 20.85/21.05 percent, down from opening's 20.90/21.20 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 21.10/21.40 percent against 21.00/21.25 percent at 0950 GMT.
